diagnoses.evidence: pe-uk 2.132.6 stamp_duty/residential/purchase/main/{subsequent,first/rate,first/max}.yaml
diagnoses.fixed_in: policyengine-uk 2.141.8 (4044d6ccf, 'Fix recent residential SDLT purchase schedules and inclusive first-buyer caps')
diagnoses.summary: pe-uk 2.132.6 has no Growth Plan SDLT relief: its 2024-25 schedule already equals the pre-relief world, so removing the relief changes nothing. The relief was law from 23 September 2022 to 31 March 2025.
The relief ended on 31 March 2025, so modern law from 2025-26 is the pre-relief world. The OBR's later costings of the increase are offset by its separate 'ending the Growth Plan change' measure.
The counterfactual keeps the relief from 2025-26, the first year the measure changes; the OBR's 2024-25 yield is timing around the end date, which an annual construction does not express.

diagnoses.evidence: data/uk/events/inventory.jsonl rows for budget_2017__class_4_nics_increase_to_10_from_april_2018_and_11_from_april_2019; FINDINGS.json group effects
diagnoses.summary: The OBR's costing is net of the self-employed incorporating in response: its NICs yield falls from £570m (2019-20) to £475m (2021-22) while income tax goes from -£60m to -£420m and corporation tax rises to +£340m. A static run has no such response. PolicyEngine's NICs leg alone (+£0.68bn in 2024-25) is 1.27 times the OBR's NICs row scaled to the modern base (£0.475bn x 1.131).

diagnoses.summary: Setting the statutory Marriage Allowance rate to 0 switches on the CPS expanded Marriage Allowance reform (reforms/cps/marriage_tax_reforms.py: 'rate != original_rate'), which keeps the 10% rate and extends eligibility to higher- and additional-rate taxpayers. So the reversal extends the allowance instead of removing it, and income tax falls. Present in 2.132.6 and 2.143.0; fixed in policyengine-uk 2.148.2 (#2553).

diagnoses.evidence: pe-uk 2.143.0 variables/gov/hmrc/income_tax/allowances/{trading_allowance_deduction,property_allowance_deduction_if_used}.py; microcosm_uk_2024_25.h5 has no self_employment_gross_receipts column
diagnoses.summary: Without gross receipts, pe-uk relieves only profits within the £1,000 allowance and treats a larger profit as already reflecting the better of expenses and the allowance (trading_allowance_deduction, property_allowance_deduction_if_used). The Microcosm UK 2024-25 cut carries no self_employment_gross_receipts, so the partial-relief leg the OBR costed has nothing to act on, and most fully relieved profits fall within the personal allowance anyway. The removal is 0.20 of the scaled OBR costing.

diagnoses.evidence: pe-uk 2.143.0 variables/household/consumption/additional_residential_property_purchased.py; microcosm changelog.d/1095-additional-property-purchases.added.md
diagnoses.summary: From policyengine-uk 2.134.1 (52030637b, fixing #2238) additional-dwelling and non-residential purchase prices are inputs, nil unless the dataset imputes them; before, every home buyer's whole stock of other residential property was charged as one additional-dwelling purchase. The interim Microcosm cut was built for 2.132.6 and does not supply the inputs, so on 2.143.0 no household buys an additional dwelling: modern-law SDLT falls from £15.0bn to £8.1bn in 2025-26 and the surcharge has nothing to act on. Microcosm imputes both from microcosm#1308 (the property_purchases stage), so the pre-Budget cut carries them. A model swap is valid only where the data carries the newer model's inputs.

diagnoses.evidence: pe-uk 52030637b; microcosm#1308
diagnoses.summary: Both sides of this change come from one model fix. 2.132.6 charges every home buyer's whole stock of other residential property at the higher rates (policyengine-uk#2238), and its scale lacks Autumn Budget 2024's further 2pp, so its £0.94bn is a 1pp removal on an overstated base. 2.143.0 has the full scale but takes the additional-dwelling purchase as a dataset input, which the interim cut does not supply, so it returns 0. Neither number is the surcharge's yield; the pre-Budget cut imputes the purchases (microcosm#1308).

diagnoses.evidence: pe-uk parameters/gov/simulation/microdata_vat_coverage.yaml (0.38 at 2.132.6; 0.469 = 0.67 x 0.7 at 2.143.0) and utils/vat.py; policyengine-uk#1996 (98ab77093) and 691267f5c, both first in 2.135.7. The modern-law VAT aggregate falls by 0.810 in both years, which is 0.38 / 0.469.
diagnoses.summary: policyengine-uk 2.135.7 splits VAT grossing into the survey's consumption coverage and the household share of receipts (0.67 x 0.7 = 0.469, replacing the combined 0.38, with the derivation in docs/engineering/vat-coverage.md). VAT on recorded consumption is divided by that factor, so every VAT effect scales by 0.810. The rate rise's scaled ratio to the OBR moves from 1.31 to 1.06.

diagnoses.evidence: pe-uk variables/gov/hmrc/income_tax/bracketized_savings_income/savings_starter_rate_income.py at 2.132.6 and 2.143.0. docs/uk_replay/evidence/policy_experiments/swap_mechanisms.py and README.md: a person with £20,000 of earnings and £3,000 of interest in 2025 keeps the whole starting-rate band on 2.132.6 (removing the allowance changes nothing) and has none on 2.143.0 (removing it costs £200).
diagnoses.fixed_in: policyengine-uk 2.139.2 (35f992c6a, 'Correct the savings starting-rate taper', fixing #1799)
diagnoses.summary: pe-uk 2.132.6 started the starting-rate taper at the personal allowance plus the £5,000 band, applied to income already net of the allowance, so it kept the whole 0% band for anyone with taxable non-savings income up to £17,570; both versions' code comments read ITA 2007 s. 12 as removing it from the first pound. Those savers' interest sat in the 0% band, where the allowance does nothing. 2.143.0 tapers from the first pound, so more interest falls in the basic and higher bands, where the allowance relieves it: the reversal's scaled ratio moves from 0.43 to 0.73.

diagnoses.evidence: pe-uk variables/gov/hmrc/income_tax/adjusted_net_income.py at 2.132.6 and 2.143.0. docs/uk_replay/evidence/policy_experiments/swap_mechanisms.py and README.md: a parent on £62,000 with £4,000 of employee pension contributions and one child has adjusted net income of £62,000 and a £135 charge on 2.132.6, £58,000 and no charge on 2.143.0.
diagnoses.fixed_in: policyengine-uk 2.134.8 (1dbc88172, 'fix: include relieved pension contributions in adjusted net income')
diagnoses.summary: ITA 2007 s. 58 deducts relieved pension contributions in adjusted net income, which sets the charge's taper. pe-uk 2.132.6 deducted only grossed-up Gift Aid, so savers' adjusted net income was too high and more of them paid the charge. 2.143.0 deducts the relief, and the charge raises £0.13bn to 0.15bn less.

diagnoses.evidence: Both populations' artifacts before and after the third review's correction: the certified pair +£1.367bn (main scale only) to +£0.949bn (all three legs) in 2025-26; the model swap +£1.341bn to +£1.341bn. docs/uk_replay/evidence/policy_experiments/sdlt_growth_plan_check.py for the per-purchase legs.
diagnoses.summary: The difference is the additional-dwellings leg. On 2.132.6 it raises tax by about £0.42bn: the construction merges the bands at current law's 5%, above that engine's 3% (no Autumn Budget 2024 +2pp, fixed in 2.141.8), on its overstated purchase base (policyengine-uk#2238). On 2.143.0 it is nil, because the interim cut carries no additional-dwelling purchases (model_swap_input_gaps; microcosm#1308). The main-scale and lease legs agree: +£1.367bn on the pair against +£1.341bn on the swap before the correction.
